new.story: A 1977 Jamaican 10 cents bearing the national coat of arms: a crocodile crest above a shield flanked by two supporters, with the motto Out of Many, One People on the scroll below. A butterfly among flowers fills the other side. It was everyday small change in Jamaica in the late 1970s.
new.notes: Obverse photo only; JAMAICA, the arms and the 1977 date were read from the photo. The denomination is not on the photographed side: it follows from the wide JAMAICA lettering of the circulation type, the copper-nickel metal, and base rates (the 1977 5 cents and the narrow-legend 10 cents were Franklin Mint collector strikes only; no 25 cents was struck in 1977; the 1 cent was aluminium). A reverse photo settles it outright.

issue.mint_text: Pessac mint; cornucopia and dolphin privy marks flank the date

new.story: A 1983 French 20 centimes, the golden everyday coin of pre-euro France. Marianne in her Phrygian cap of liberty is on the other side; the big 20 on this side sits inside a wreath of laurel and wheat.
new.notes: Reverse photo only; LIBERTE EGALITE FRATERNITE, the big 20, CENTIMES and the engraver signature A. DIEUDONNE were read from the photo. The date was read digit by digit from an enlarged crop as 1983 (a first glance at the small photo suggested 1963; the enlargement shows the third digit is an 8). The dolphin privy mark to the right of the date is the Paris mark used 1975-94.
